title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
An automated license plate camera alert was treated as a confirmed identification of a vehicle, and an armed stop followed on the strength of a resemblance rather than a verified plate match. The camera's output was a flag on a car linked to aggravated robberies, not a sighting of that car, and the distinction was lost before anyone approached the men.

The failure sits at the handoff between the camera alert and the field stop. Deputies and the helicopter could not read the plates on the car in front of them, which was the one check that would have separated the flagged Camaro from the one Anthony and Julian were driving. The stop went ahead with at least five patrol cars, a helicopter, guns pointed and both men handcuffed, and the mistake was recognised only after the handcuffing.

What is not established is whether department procedures were followed. The sheriff's office has said supervisors will review body camera video, and no finding from that review has been reported. The men were not charged, and the internal affairs complaint and the attorney Anthony's mother plans to hire are steps being taken, not conclusions about fault.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
In Cypress, Texas, Harris County sheriff's deputies stopped two men, Anthony and Julian, both 19, on Aug. 3 after mistaking their Camaro for a stolen car. The men had just returned from a gas station when at least five patrol cars and a helicopter surrounded them. Deputies pointed guns, forced Julian to the ground, and handcuffed both men. The sheriff's office said license plate cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a similar car, but deputies and the helicopter could not read its plates, so backup was called.

After handcuffing the men, deputies realized they had the wrong car. The men were not charged. The sheriff's office said supervisors, including the district captain and shift lieutenants and sergeants, will review body camera video to check whether procedures were followed. The men were told how to file a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so. Anthony's mother said she plans to hire an attorney.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
